text:
andrea: quick heads-up — vuln scanner flagged openssl CVE-2026-9999 in our base image `gcr.io/redwood/base:2026-03-22`. severity: CRITICAL.

samir: can you paste the layer sha and scanner excerpt?

andrea: layer: sha256:fa12...bbcc. scanner: `CVE-2026-9999 | openssl 3.0.6 | RCE | CVSS 9.8` — appears in /usr/lib/libssl.so.
maria: even if upstream, we should rebuild a patched base to control final artifact and strip tooling. also need longer audit retention for signing/KMS events during the window.
julian: KMS note — do not revoke key versions until verification is clean. cosign verifies against the key version in the signature.

security-oncall: propose immediate steps:
- pause new canaries
- build patched base in staging with distro patch + binary stripping
- cosign sign with current key version (no rotation yet)
- 1% canary 30m, monitor cosign verify + startup logs
- if green, ramp
assign owners?

samir: I'll run canary watch and open IAM MR to grant CI-SA temporary signer role.

andrea: I'll kick the staging build now.
build-bot: build: staging/base:2026-03-22-patched #4712 started.
maria: filing SIEM retention PR to extend image-sign and KMS logs from 30d -> 180d. link when created.

security-oncall: logging owners: andrea(build), samir(canary+IAM), maria(audit). i'll coordinate with infra-oncall. post cosign logs here once available.

andrea: staged image built, cosign attest OK. scheduling canary at 16:10 UTC 1% traffic. samir on watch. :thumbsup:

security-oncall: keep thread pinned to incident. if cosign verification errors pop up, escalate immediately.
